page: Microsoft Azure M8-2ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MS server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 219.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a high memory-to-core ratio of 109.38 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 262 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark data indicates significant performance tradeoffs, particularly regarding compute capabilities. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place this instance in the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read-only large block bandwidth measured at 9.62 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 8.08 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations (1.27 million operations per second) similarly fall into the lowest performance tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M8-2ms offers high memory density relative to its low vCPU count, making it suitable for workloads requiring massive memory footprints without intensive computational demands. However, the low CPU performance and restricted memory bandwidth represent a major tradeoff for processing-heavy tasks. This server is appropriate for memory-bound, low-compute workloads such as large in-memory caching, small database hosting with high RAM requirements, or legacy applications requiring substantial memory allocation but minimal CPU utilization.
